instruction: Seeking help with English learning. Would you be so kind as to create a practice exercise for me?
output:
Complete this sentence: "I _____ my homework before I go out." (a) finish, b) will finish, c) am finishing, d) have finished 


The correct option is **(c) am finising**. The other options are incorrect because they do not follow the present continuous tense of verbs in an active voice structure. This type of verb construction emphasizes that something is happening at the moment when it's being spoken/written about. For example, if someone says “I’m going”, then we know that action has already been completed but still remains relevant within the context of conversation. In contrast, saying “will” implies future actions which would make sense only if there was some sort of prediction involved such as asking what one might expect from another person based upon their past behavior - e.g., “Will he come?”  This makes use of modal auxiliary verbs like ‘going’, ‘have gone’, etc. However, since no predictions were made here, 'am finishing' fits best into the given situation. Therefore, the right choice should always depend on whether any form of predicting behaviour exists between two people speaking together. If none does exist, using simple tenses can provide more accurate results than complex ones. So next time your teacher asks you to complete sentences by choosing among different forms of verbs

instruction: Hi, I'd like to learn to bake challah. Can you give me a recipe for that?
output: Ingredients: 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 2 teaspoons sugar, 3 eggs, ½ cup warm water, ¼ cup vegetable oil, ⅓ cup butter (melted), two tablespoons of active dry yeast. Instructions: In large bowl mix together flours, salt, and sugar until combined. Make well in center with your fingertip then pour in egg mixture, melted butter, and dissolved yeast into it. Knead dough by hand using wooden spoon about five minutes before adding extra tablespoonful of olive oil at once every minute while kneading till smooth ball is formed. Place covered container filled with oiled cloth over top of mixing bowl and let rise overnight. After rising place onto greased baking sheet lined parchment paper spread out evenly. Bake uncovered at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for approximately thirty minutes. Enjoy!

instruction: I'm interested in baking challah and would appreciate if you could provide me with a recipe.
output: Ingredients: 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 2 teaspoons sugar, 3 eggs, ½ cup warm water, ¼ cup vegetable oil, two tablespoons of active dry yeast (or one packet), three large applesauce containers filled with butter to grease an oven pan. Instructions: In a bowl mix together four cups of flour, one tablespoon of salt, two teaspoons of sugar, and half a cup of warm water until it forms into dough. Knead for five minutes then let rest covered at room temperature for thirty minutes. Roll out onto lightly floured surface and cut circles about six inches wide using cookie cutters. Place them in greased muffin tins and cover loosely with plastic wrap. Let rise again while preparing your filling - heat up some apple sauce in saucepan over medium high heat stirring occasionally until bubbly around edges but still slightly thick. Once risen place each circle carefully back into their tin molds and fill generously with hot apple mixture. Bake uncovered at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for twenty minutes before serving. Enjoy!

instruction: Could you share a recipe for baking challah? I'm keen on learning how to make it.
output: Ingredients: 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 2 teaspoons sugar, 3 eggs, ½ cup warm water, ¼ cup vegetable oil, ⅓ cup butter (melted), two tablespoons of active dry yeast. Instructions: In large bowl mix together flours, salt, sugar, egg yolks, and melted butter until combined. Add in lukewarm water slowly while mixing with your hands. Knead dough by hand for about five minutes then place into greased bowl cover tightly wrap up and let rise at room temperature for one hour. Punch down dough roll out onto lightly oiled surface spread evenly with softened butter cut into strips braid them around each other form rolls bake uncovered over medium heat for thirty minutes check doneness before serving Enjoy!

instruction: Please supply a challah baking recipe; I'm eager to learn the process.
output: Ingredients: 1 cup warm water, two teaspoons of sugar, one teaspoon of active dry yeast, three cups all-purpose flour, four tablespoons butter (melted), one egg yolk beaten with an ounce of milk, salt, oil for greasing pan. Instructions: In a large bowl mix together the warm water and sugar until dissolved then stir in the yeast. Let stand five minutes before adding the flour gradually mixing it into the mixture as you go along. Add melted butter, beat eggs/milk combination, and finally sprinkle some salt over top. Knead dough by hand about ten times. Place onto greased surface and knead another few more times. Roll out flat and cut shapes using cookie cutters if desired. Bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for approximately thirty minutes till golden brown. Enjoy!

instruction: I'm looking to expand my baking skills by making challah. Do you have a recipe for it?
output: Ingredients: 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 2 teaspoons sugar, 3 eggs, ½ cup warm water, ¼ cup vegetable oil, 6 tablespoons butter (melted), two packages active dry yeast. Instructions: In large bowl mix together flours, salt, sugar, one egg, half of the melted butter, and three quarters of the warm water until combined. Let stand in refrigerator overnight. The next day combine remaining ingredients into dough mixture and knead with hands for five minutes. Place dough ball onto greased surface and roll out flat. Cut shapes using cookie cutters if desired. Bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for about twenty minutes before serving. Enjoy!

instruction: Teach me how to bake challah bread by providing a reliable recipe, please.
output: Ingredients: 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 teaspoon salt, 2 teaspoons sugar, 3 tablespoons active dry yeast, ½ cup warm water, ¼ cup vegetable oil, two eggs plus one egg yolk for brushing dough with glaze (optional), poppy seeds, sesame seeds, cinnamon, nutmeg as desired toppings. Instructions: In large bowl mix together flours, salt, sugar, and yeast until combined. Add in warm water slowly while mixing continuously. Stir in olive oil then gradually incorporate beaten eggs into mixture. Knead dough onto lightly oiled surface for about five minutes before placing it back into greased bowl covered tightly with plastic wrap. Let rise at room temperature for an hour. instruction: Why can time seem to slow down in dangerous situations?
output: Time seems to move slower when we are experiencing a stressful situation because our bodies release adrenaline, which slows down brain activity and makes us feel more relaxed while under pressure. This allows for better decision-making but also leads to an increased perception of how long it takes before something happens. Additionally, people tend to focus their attention solely on what is happening at that moment rather than looking ahead into the future, making them perceive events as taking longer due to lack of perspective. Finally, some studies have shown that fear triggers changes in neurochemicals such as dopamine and norepinephrine, leading to slowed reaction times and heightened awareness of danger. All these factors combine to make time appear to pass slowly during moments of stress.

instruction: What is the explanation for time perception appearing to decelerate during hazardous events?
output: The phenomenon of slowed-down perceptions in dangerous situations can be explained by a combination of physiological, psychological, and cognitive factors such as increased arousal levels due to stress hormones like adrenaline which slows down reaction times, heightened focus that makes it difficult to process information quickly enough, decreased attention span caused by fear responses, and an altered sense of self awareness leading to reduced decision making capabilities. Additionally, people may also experience tunnel vision when they are under duress, focusing only on immediate threats while ignoring other potential dangers around them. This combined effect creates what appears to be slower processing speeds than usual. Furthermore, some studies have shown that individuals who perceive danger tend to overestimate their own ability to escape from harm compared to those without this perceived threat. Therefore, even if there was no actual change in response speed, one might still feel more vulnerable because of how much faster our minds seem to move away from any possible risk. Finally, research has found evidence suggesting that certain types of stimuli associated with imminent death (such as loud noises) cause us to become hypervigilant - meaning we pay closer attention to anything happening near us at all times. As these reactions occur rapidly, so too does the feeling of being overwhelmed and disoriented. All together, these various effects create the illusion of slowness experienced during moments of high tension.

instruction: How does time manage to seemingly crawl when one faces peril?

Additionally, this heightened state of alertness makes everything seem slower since there's less room for distractions such as daydreaming or other activities that take up mental energy. Finally, some people may also experience physical symptoms like increased heart rate due to their body’s fight-or-flight response during times of danger, further contributing to how quickly they perceive time passing. All these factors combine together to make time feel much longer while under duress.

instruction: What causes the sensation of time moving more slowly when in threatening circumstances?

The experience suggests we may be able to better manage stress by becoming mindful of how quickly things seem to pass. Additionally, some research indicates this effect could help explain why certain activities like meditation appear so effective at reducing anxiety levels. instruction:
Give a brief explanation of the requested part of the paper.

Paper: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.
Explain: The dominant sequence transduction models
output: The Dominant Sequence Transduction Models (DSTMs) is composed of Recurrent Neural Networks which use encoders and decoders connected via Attention Mechanisms. These DSTMs have been used extensively due to their high performance but they require significant computational resources as compared to simpler architectures such as Transformers. In this research we introduce a novel Architecture called "Transformer" using only Attention Mechanism without any Recurrence or Convolutional layers. This allows us to achieve better accuracy than previous methods at lower cost when trained on larger datasets like those found in Machine Translation Tasks where one can leverage multiple parallel processing units simultaneously. Furthermore, since no recurrences were required during Training, the Model was able to complete its Task faster resulting in improved efficiency. As demonstrated by experiments conducted on various language pairs, the proposed transformer achieved higher scores than previously reported benchmarks even surpassing ensemble approaches. Additionally, successful application has been made possible across different domains thanks to its ability to generalize easily between languages and types of problems. Thus far, transformers appear promising candidates for future development given their potential advantages regarding speed, scalability and effectiveness.

instruction: At what point in the brewing procedure are hops incorporated?

Additionally, hop additions vary from one brewery to another based on their own recipes. | Column Name | Type     |
| personId          | int         |
| lastName         | varchar |

personId is the primary key column for this table.
This table contains information about the ID of some persons and their first and last names.

| Column Name | Type     |
| addressId        | int         |
| personId          | int         |
| city                   | varchar|
| state                | varchar |
addressId is the primary key column for this table.

Write an SQL query to report the first name, last name, city, and state of each person in the Person table. If the address of a personId is not present in the Address table, report null instead.

Implementation:
select FirstName, LastName, City, State
from Person left join Address
on Person.PersonId = Address.PersonId
;

This allows us to retrieve both columns (FirstName,LastName) as well as additional details such as City and State which can then be combined into a single output record containing First/Last Names along with corresponding Cities and States. Additionally, since no specific condition was specified when joining these two tables, it returns NULL values where records do not exist within either table. Thus providing accurate results even without specifying conditions like WHERE clauses would have done otherwise. Finally, by using SELECT statement we ensure only relevant fields are returned while still maintaining clarity through proper syntax. Therefore, our solution provides efficient way to access desired data quickly and accurately.

On this special occasion many people take time out from work and school to attend parades, visit historical sites related to presidential events, watch speeches by current politicians, participate in community service projects, give thanks for those serving our government today, and more! In addition, some states hold “President’s Days” which are similar celebrations held throughout the year honoring different figures such as Abraham Lincoln and Thomas Jefferson. These days often feature activities like flag-raising ceremonies, patriotic music performances, reenactments of important moments during these president’s lives, educational programs focused around them, etc., making President’s Day one of America’s most celebrated holidays each February 15th.

instruction: Could you shed light on Presidents' Day and its importance?
output: Presidents’ Day is an annual holiday in honor of George Washington, who was elected as America’s first president in 1789. It celebrates his leadership during a time when there were no laws to govern the country yet he established many precedents that are still followed today such as setting up Congress and establishing neutrality with foreign countries. The day also honors all presidents since then by recognizing their contributions to American democracy. On this special occasion people often visit monuments dedicated to past leaders like Mount Vernon (George Washington) and other historical sites related to presidential history. Additionally it serves as a reminder for citizens about how important voting rights are – something President Lincoln emphasized throughout his presidency. Finally, some states have designated February 20th as “Washington Birthday” which marks another way Americans celebrate Presidential History!

instruction: Inform me about the observance of Presidents' Day and its significance.
output: Presidents’ Day is an annual federal holiday in the United States that honors all U.S presidents, both past and present. It was first established as a day to honor George Washington by President Woodrow Wilson in 1971 but has since been expanded to include other former presidents who have served during their terms. The date for this celebration falls annually on the third Monday of February each year. This makes it one of only two holidays celebrated every year which fall outside of January (the second being Memorial Day). On this special occasion Americans celebrate with parades, speeches from local officials honoring those they serve alongside family gatherings at home. Additionally many businesses are closed so people can take time off work to spend quality time together celebrating our nation’s leaders!

instruction: I like to host guests at my home from time to time, and I am gathering  recipes of different dishes and drinks to keep things interesting. I am interested in trying some Indonesian dishes. Can you give me a recipe for Tahu Gejrot Cirebon?
output: Tahu gejrot cirebon is an Indonesian dish made with fried tofu cubes that are coated in sweet soy sauce-based marinade before being deep-fried until crispy. The ingredients include 1 block firm silken tofu (cut into small pieces), ½ cup tapioca flour, ¼ teaspoon ground turmeric powder, ¾ tablespoon sugar, two tablespoons kecap manis (sweet soy sauce), one clove garlic minced, three cloves shallots finely chopped, four teaspoons vegetable oil, salt to taste, and water as needed. To make this dish: first mix together all dry spices except the sesame seeds then set aside. Heat up the cooking oil over medium heat and fry each piece of tofu cube till golden brown. Remove them out onto paper towels to drain off excess oil. In another bowl combine the remaining wet ingredients including half of the spice mixture and whisk it well. Add the cooked tofu back into the pan along with any leftover juices/oil left behind. Stir everything around so that every side gets evenly covered by the glaze. Cook through stirring occasionally until desired consistency has been reached. Finally sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and serve hot! Enjoy your delicious Tahu Gejoret Cirebon!

instruction: I'm in need of a recipe for Tahu Gejrot Cirebon to serve my guests, since I enjoy inviting people over and trying out different culinary delights, with a focus on Indonesian recipes.
output: Tahu gejrot cirebon is an Indonesian dish made from deep-fried tofu that has been coated in flour then fried until golden brown. The ingredients include 250g firm silken tofu cut into cubes, ½ cup all purpose flour, ¼ teaspoon salt, two tablespoons vegetable oil, one tablespoon water, three cloves garlic minced, four shallots diced, five chilies sliced thinly, six pieces galangal grated, half onion chopped finely, eight slices tempeh, seven cups coconut milk, and ten grams sugar. To make this dish: first heat up some oil in a pan at medium temperature. Then mix together the flour, salt, and spices (garlic, shallot, chili, and galangal) in a bowl. Dip each cube of tofu in the mixture before frying it lightly till crispy. Next fry the tempeh separately using similar method as above. In another pot bring the coconut milk to boil while stirring occasionally. Add onions and cook them briefly. Finally pour everything back onto the hot oil and stir continuously so that no lumps form. Cook for about 1 minute more and your tahu goreng cirebon should be ready! Enjoy serving warm alongside rice.

Heat oil over medium heat in a wok/pan and fry the cubed tofu till they are lightly browned all around. Remove out onto paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve hot! instruction: explain the basics of area and perimeter
output: Area is a measure of space enclosed within an object, while perimeter measures the total length around its boundary. Area can be calculated by multiplying width times height (e.g., for squares), whereas perimeter involves adding up all sides lengths together to get one number that represents how long it would take to walk along each side's edge in order to completely encircle the shape from end-to-end. For example, if you have two equal sized rectangles with 4 units wide and 6 units high then their areas are both 24 square units but they will also share a common perimeter which equals 10 units when measured across them diagonally. This means there must be at least four lines connecting opposite corners so as to form this diagonal path between any pair of points inside either rectangle without crossing over into another line segment outside those boundaries. The same principle applies even more strongly to polygons such as triangles where only three edges need to connect vertices instead of four like quadrilaterals do - thus making calculations easier than ever before! Finally remember: no matter what type of figure we’re dealing with – whether rectangular shapes or irregular ones – calculating these measurements always requires understanding basic geometry principles first. So don’t forget your compass next time you want to explore some spatial relationships further!
